function: ENSAC deep RL agent jointly selects served UE, UAV trajectory, task offloading ratio, and UAV transmit power to minimize weighted energy and delay cost (p. 6).
system: K=5 UEs, one UAV at 100 m (relay and server), fixed MEC; G2A uses OFDMA, LoS or blocked; 1 MHz links; antennas, carrier not stated (pp. 4, 8).
method: Soft actor-critic variant (ENSAC): actor plus two Q critics and V critic with target, ReLU DNNs, Adam; reinforcement learning with replay buffer and entropy-normalized reward (pp. 7-8).
data_channel: No dataset: Python simulation, LoS gain alpha0/d^2 with blockage indicator and 20 dB loss, UEs moving randomly in a 100 m square; Table I (pp. 4, 8).
test_conditions: Training curves under learning rates and exploration noise; converged cost swept over weights, total task size, UE number (1-9), computing resources; no separate unseen test scenario stated (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: random UAV flight trajectory and all tasks computed on UAV. Learned: DDPG and TD3, both with normalized state and reward (pp. 8-9).
metrics: Total system cost (weighted energy and delay) and its percentage reduction, energy consumption, execution delay, convergence over epochs (pp. 1, 9-10).
q1_support: p. 4: "where α0 denotes the channel gain at a reference distance"; a custom LoS gain alpha0/d^2 with a blockage loss, not 3GPP TR 38.811, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "Using the total system cost results obtained after the algorithm convergence" for each task size and UE number; the paper never states that a trained agent is tested on an unseen setting or adapted.
q3_support: p. 10: "compared with the TD3, DDPG, UAV-RFT, and UAV-ALL methods, the ENSAC algorithm reduces the total system cost by an average of 38.24%, 56.53%, 68.88%, and 72.91%".
q4_support: p. 7: "thus improving the rate of convergence and stability"; only a convergence claim, with no order of complexity, operations, parameters or runtime reported anywhere.
q5_support: p. 8: "Python is used for simulation"; simulated environment with parameters in Table I, no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset or measurement.
notes: Included as area 6, a borderline case: the title is task offloading for UAV-assisted MEC, but the agent also learns the UAV transmit power p_n(i) jointly with scheduling, trajectory and offloading ratio (p. 6, action A(i); the abstract on p. 1 names power allocation), so under the aerial-link rule it passes above_phy and NTN admits single-antenna links. Only system cost is evaluated, no link-level metric. Table I was read from PDF page 8; antennas and carrier frequency are not stated.
